operability_evidence_tiers.exact_current_production_qualified: Exact-current production-path evidence references are attached to the feature record; P10 still validates the controlling evidence before admission.
operability_evidence_tiers.signed_supporting: Signed or live installed-product evidence exists, but it is not final qualification of the exact current clean source and complete installed stack.
operability_evidence_tiers.production_component: Executable production code is covered at a component, process, HTTP, persistence, or protocol boundary, but exact-current signed end-to-end qualification remains open.
operability_evidence_tiers.fixture_or_source_only: Current evidence is fixture, synthetic-host, in-process, source, visibility-only, or otherwise does not execute the complete production path.
operability_evidence_tiers.broken_or_absent: An advertised production path is absent, disabled, or known inoperative and remains release-blocking.

operability_summary.interpretation: Feature inventory, parity classification, source presence, tools/list visibility, and unit or fixture coverage are not proof that a feature works through the shipped production path.
open_release_blockers: protected filesystem signed mutation, bounded quarantine verification, recovery, and full atomic-swap adversarial matrix
clean-install managed-provider configuration, credentials, probe, and autonomy
native UI signing, Developer Mode, protected-service lifecycle, and production-control qualification
real-provider forced rollover, exact successor acknowledgement, predecessor fencing, automatic continuation, GUI-closed operation, and complete crash-state recovery
exact-current shell, manager restart, additive-tool, migration, and complete advertised MCP tool execution
operability_summary.qualification_rule: Only exact_current_production_qualified is eligible for P10 completion, and that tier closes no gate by itself. Every feature must carry an evidence reference that the controlling gate command accepts against the exact current source.

required_runtime_surfaces.requirement: The 66 preserved and 38 additive classifications establish current source-surface coverage only. They are not runtime, security, signing, hardware, continuity, or release-completion claims.

Every advertised tool must execute successfully through the current production authorization and transport path, with its established result contract preserved; a tools/list descriptor or in-process synthetic invocation is insufficient.

The currently advertised-but-unqualified fs_move and recursive directory fs_delete operations must operate through the signed privileged service, remain fail-closed without it, and pass the full atomic-swap adversarial identity-race matrix. Mitigation must not be described as race elimination.

A clean installation must create or expose a supported production control that writes and validates managed-providers/forge.native-session-host/lmstudio-provider.json before provider probe or autonomy can be considered operable.

Advertised controls must be visible, controllable, persistent across app and manager restart, and verified in a coherent current-source signed build. One fixture-backed or single-control XCUI result does not qualify this surface.

A real LM Studio request must trigger threshold rollover, exact successor acknowledgement, predecessor fencing, automatic continuation, GUI-closed operation, and crash-state recovery. Unit, fixture, and synthetic-host tests are not substitutes.
The final signed app, embedded manager, helper, configuration migrations, and recovery paths must be qualified together from the same source commit.
Resource budgets, long-running behavior, and release installation must receive operator-owned real-hardware qualification; source and synthetic tests do not complete this deferred gate.

known_environment_limits.detail: fs_move and recursive directory fs_delete remain advertised but are not qualified as executable through the signed privileged-service path. The descriptor-relative and quarantine logic mitigates named-path races but does not establish identity-conditional mutation or eliminate the residual race.

The recorded evidence covers one protected-service Settings control test only. It does not qualify final signing, Developer Mode behavior, service enable/disable/reinstall, daemon routing, restart recovery, or the adversarial mutation matrix.

The provider adapter loads managed-providers/forge.native-session-host/lmstudio-provider.json when present, but the current production app, CLI, and manager routes do not create that file on a clean installation. Fixture and manually provisioned configurations do not close this route gap.

The source contains real-provider acceptance coverage, but this inventory refresh did not execute or accept it. Exact successor acknowledgement, predecessor fencing, automatic continuation, GUI-closed operation, and crash-state recovery remain unqualified.

A bounded single-control XCUI record is not the complete signed production-manager navigation, settings, provider, project, runtime, continuity, restart, and accessibility matrix. Native UI and signing remain deferred and release-blocking.

Source and unit coverage preserve shell_exec separately from additive clean-profile runtime tools, but the cited installed-stack qualification exited 4. Final coherent app-and-manager restart operability and result-contract evidence remain required.
Real-hardware release qualification is operator-deferred. No unit, fixture, synthetic-host, or source inventory result marks hardware coverage complete.
